newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab League criticises U.S. veto on Israel homes.
newsitem.headline: Arab League criticises U.S. veto on Israel homes.

text.p: The Arab League said on Sunday the United States contradicted its own reaction to Israel's plans to build a new Jewish neighborhood in Arab East Jerusalem by vetoing a U.N. draft resolution against the project.
Washington on Friday vetoed the draft -- backed by the U.N. Security Council's other 14 members -- calling on Israel to abandon plans to build 6,500 homes in the disputed city.

"The non-endorsement of the U.N. resolution because of the U.S. veto contradicts (U.S. President Bill) Clinton's remarks preceding it, and contradicts the former U.S. position in the United Nations which said settlements were illegal and form an obstacle to peace," the Arab League said in a statement.
The 22-member, Cairo-based league cited Clinton's remarks during Palestinian President Yasser Araft visit to Washington last week.

Clinton, commenting on the Israeli cabinet's decision to authorise the housing plan, told reporters at the start of his talks with Arafat at the White House last Monday: "I would have preferred the decision not have been made because I don't think it builds confidence. I think it builds mistrust."

Palestinians, who want East Jerusalem to be the capital of a future Palestinian state, view Israeli building there as pre-empting talks on the city's status that are to be part of final peace negotiations due to be completed by 1999.
The Arab League said it backed moves by non-aligned and Arab countries in the United Nation opposing the Israeli plan.
